title: Build the shared e2e test harness and NDJSON logging library
description:
GOAL
Create scripts/e2e/lib.sh (structured-logging bash library), scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (discovers and runs every scripts/e2e/*.sh test, aggregates NDJSON logs, prints a machine-readable summary), and the conventions every later e2e subtask in this graph builds on.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Every vertical slice in this project must prove itself with end-to-end evidence, and the constitution requires that evidence to be replayable and machine-inspectable — a wall of unstructured stdout is not evidence. One shared harness means every e2e script logs identically, failures always carry enough context to replay (seeds, digests, exact commands), and run_all.sh becomes the single local entry point the verify.sh `full` lane will eventually call instead of its current typed dormant refusal (exit 3).

DELIVERABLES
- scripts/e2e/lib.sh: step(), assert_eq(), assert_file_digest(), with_seed(), log-to-NDJSON functions; every step line carries ts/script/step/cmd/exit/duration_ms/artifact_digests/seed/note.
- scripts/e2e/run_all.sh: runs all scripts/e2e/*.sh except lib, collects per-script NDJSON into e2e-logs/<timestamp>/, emits a summary JSON {scripts, steps, passed, failed, wall_ms}, exit nonzero on any failure.
- A trivial self-test script scripts/e2e/harness_selftest.sh exercising every lib function including the failure path (run in a subshell so the suite still passes).
- Documentation of the conventions in a comment header of lib.sh (the canonical reference; no separate doc to drift).

ACCEPTANCE
- harness_selftest.sh passes and demonstrably exercises the failure path with the context dump;
- run_all.sh aggregates >=1 script and its summary JSON parses with python3 -m json.tool;
- logs are valid NDJSON (each line parses independently);
- shellcheck-clean or explicitly annotated; bash -n clean; set -euo pipefail everywhere;
- ./scripts/verify.sh fast stays green (the harness adds no Rust surface).

NON-GOALS
- No test content for real subsystems here (later beads own that); no CI wiring (workflow YAML stays a thin adapter).

FUTURE-SELF NOTES
The full/release lanes must keep refusing (exit 3) until real engine lanes exist — do NOT wire run_all.sh into verify.sh full as a green path while the suite is trivial; that would be exactly the false-green NEG-012 rejects.

CONSTITUTIONAL CONSTRAINTS (AGENTS.md; non-negotiable)
- Pure Rust, edition 2024, dated-nightly pin from rust-toolchain.toml; every first-party crate carries #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; no C/C++ FFI, no C Git/libgit2/JGit/Dulwich/gix, no hidden subprocess fallback. Upstream Git binaries are pinned, sandboxed differential ORACLES only (never production).
- Asupersync is the sole async runtime (no Tokio/async-std/smol). Long-lived work owns children via regions; cancellation is request -> drain -> finalize; effects use typed obligations (Reserved -> Committed -> Acknowledged, or Reserved -> Aborted).
- Closed dependency universe: every crate (incl. transitive, enforced via Cargo.lock scan) must match an active allow row in registries/dependency_policy.tsv. No build scripts/proc macros without a constitutional exception. No network during builds.
- Final-abstraction slices only: no empty crates, no HashMap-pretending-to-be-storage, no fixture-only parser wired as production API. A subset is fine when its unsupported surface is a typed refusal.
- Claim lattice (invariant > proof > bounded model > statistical > SLO > benchmark): never describe this work as stronger than its evidence. Record disproven hypotheses in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md + registries/negative_evidence.tsv.
- Run ./scripts/verify.sh fast before and after; stage only intended files; keep generated artifacts out of source.

E2E LOGGING CONVENTIONS (mandatory for every e2e script)
- Scripts live in scripts/e2e/, are bash with `set -euo pipefail`, and source scripts/e2e/lib.sh (built by the e2e-harness bead).
- Every step emits one NDJSON line to the log file AND stderr: {"ts":..., "script":..., "step":..., "cmd":..., "exit":..., "duration_ms":..., "artifact_digests":{...}, "seed":..., "note":...}.
- Assertions log expected vs actual on failure and dump the relevant state directory listing + last 50 log lines of the process under test before exiting nonzero.
- Deterministic seeds are logged and settable via env so any failure replays exactly.
- A final summary line reports steps run/passed/failed and total wall time; exit code is the number of failed steps capped at 1.

title: Build the pinned upstream-Git differential-oracle harness
description:
GOAL
A sandboxed harness that downloads/pins exact upstream Git versions (recorded by version + binary digest), runs them ONLY in conformance lanes, captures byte-level transcripts (pkt-line exchanges, pack bytes, exit codes, stderr classes), and provides a comparison library that diffs FrankenGit behavior against oracle behavior with typed classifications (byte-equal / semantically-equal-declared / divergent).

WHY / BACKGROUND
The constitution forbids upstream Git in any production path but REQUIRES it as the differential oracle for compatibility claims (AGENTS.md §6; dependency_policy.tsv DEP-012 external_oracle). Every Git-facing slice (object core, pack reader/writer, upload-pack, receive-pack, the e2e slice) needs the same pinned-oracle machinery; building it once prevents each slice from inventing its own slightly-different comparison semantics — which is how false compatibility claims are born.

DELIVERABLES
- tools/git-oracle/ scripts: fetch-and-pin (records url, version, sha256 into a checked-in pin manifest), sandbox-run wrapper (no network, temp HOME, explicit env allowlist), transcript capture (client<->server byte logs), and compare library emitting NDJSON verdicts.
- Pin manifest format documented in-file; at least two pinned Git versions (one older, one current) because negotiation behavior differs across versions and the compatibility matrix declares per-version targets.
- Integration with the e2e harness logging conventions (fg000a).

ACCEPTANCE
- Harness runs a pinned Git binary fully sandboxed (no network, no user config leakage — proven by a probe test);
- transcripts are reproducible byte-for-byte for a deterministic fixture repo;
- comparison verdicts are typed and machine-readable, never a bare diff dump;
- the pin manifest records exact digests and the harness refuses a binary whose digest mismatches (fail closed);
- nothing under tools/git-oracle/ is reachable from production code (no Cargo dependency edge; shell/tooling only).

NON-GOALS
- No conformance corpus content here (owned by the Git-slice beads); no CI execution.

FUTURE-SELF NOTES
Network acquisition happens at harness SETUP time by a human/agent running the fetch script, never during builds (no-network-during-builds rule). If an environment cannot download, the pin manifest lets another machine supply the binaries out of band and verify digests.

title: FG-001 completion: emit verification replay artifacts from local lanes
description:
GOAL
Complete the last open acceptance item of backlog FG-001 (the constitutional registries + checker are already implemented and green): every ./scripts/verify.sh lane run emits a replay artifact recording source tree state (HEAD + dirty-file digest), toolchain (rustc -V), exact command, exit code, duration, and a digest of the checker report.

WHY / BACKGROUND
FG-001's other acceptance items landed with fgit-registry-check (registries reject duplicate/unsorted IDs, bad schemas, unknown statuses; unsafe/FFI/foreign-Git/build-script violations fail closed; links/fences/TxId-uniqueness/workflow rules are mechanical). What is missing is the EVIDENCE side: a green run currently leaves no artifact, so a claim that "the lane passed at revision X" is unverifiable prose — precisely what the claim lattice forbids. The replay artifact is the smallest unit of the evidence-envelope discipline (plan §34.1) applied to our own tooling.

DELIVERABLES
- verify.sh writes evidence/verify/<utc-timestamp>-<lane>.json (git-ignored directory; evidence/ added to .gitignore) with: lane, command line, HEAD commit, dirty status + digest-of-diff, rustc/cargo versions, exit code, wall time, and sha256 of captured stdout+stderr.
- --no-artifact escape hatch for tight loops; artifact writing must never change the lane exit code (failure to write = warning to stderr).
- The artifact schema documented in a comment in verify.sh (single source).

ACCEPTANCE
- Running docs/constitution/fast each produce a parseable artifact; full/release produce one recording the typed exit-3 refusal;
- artifact digests are stable for identical input state;
- a unit-style probe (scripts/e2e/verify_artifact_probe.sh, using fg000a conventions) validates schema and the exit-code-preservation rule;
- verify.sh remains bash -n clean and the fast lane stays green.

FUTURE-SELF NOTES
Do not put artifacts in the repo or registries — they are per-run evidence, not canonical state. When the Rust xtask era arrives, this logic migrates into the checker with the same schema.

title: Checker: implement version-universe and constellation.lock verification
description:
GOAL
Implement the VERIFY_SPEC §5.2 items currently and honestly documented as "join the lane as machinery lands": version-universe consistency checking and the constellation.lock evidence manifest gate for FrankenSuite sibling dependencies.

WHY / BACKGROUND
The dependency constitution (docs/DEPENDENCY_AND_MEMORY_SAFETY_CONSTITUTION.md) requires that before the first release-facing build consuming a sibling crate (asupersync, frankensqlite, ...), its exact revision, feature set, public contract, unsafe inventory, and claim level be pinned in a checked-in constellation.lock verified by the registry checker. Today zero sibling dependencies exist, so the gate is vacuous — but the moment FG-011 lands (Asupersync runtime profile) this bead becomes load-bearing. Building it BEFORE the first sibling is admitted means the gate exists on day one of real dependencies instead of being retrofitted.

DELIVERABLES
- constellation.lock TOML schema: per-sibling {name, git revision or version, feature set, unsafe_inventory_digest, claim_level, contract_notes} — documented in the file header;
- fgit-registry-check constitution lane: verifies every FrankenSuite-family dependency in Cargo.lock has a constellation row, versions match exactly, and one compatible constellation (no two rows pinning conflicting sibling revisions);
- typed errors for missing row, version drift, and unknown sibling.

ACCEPTANCE

title: Checker: empty-crate/placeholder detection and transitive-unsafe ledger
description:
GOAL
Implement the remaining honest gaps in the constitution lane: (a) empty-crate / placeholder-abstraction detection ("no empty engine crate or placeholder durable abstraction" — currently only a review obligation), and (b) the transitive-unsafe evidence ledger (recording, per external dependency, its transitive unsafe surface and pointing at the audit evidence).

WHY / BACKGROUND
The final-abstraction doctrine (AGENTS.md §4) bans empty scaffolds and fake substitutes, and today nothing mechanical enforces it — a workspace member with an empty lib.rs and a TODO would pass every gate. Similarly the dependency policy demands "ledgered_transitive" unsafe review for allowed crates, but with zero dependencies the ledger format does not even exist yet. Both become real the moment engine crates land, and both are cheap to build now while the workspace is one crate.

DELIVERABLES
- Checker: for every workspace member, refuse crate roots whose non-comment/non-attribute source is empty or only `todo!()`/`unimplemented!()` bodies (heuristic is fine; document it); refuse `pub struct X;` + no impl "marker scaffolds" only when the crate has no tests and no other items (conservative — avoid false positives on genuine marker types).
- registries/unsafe_ledger.tsv schema (id, crate_pattern, transitive_unsafe_summary, audit_evidence, status) + checker validation wired into the registry framework; rows required for every allow_fundamental/allow_by_audit dependency present in Cargo.lock.
- Registry README updated.

ACCEPTANCE
- Fixture probes prove: empty-lib crate fails; todo-only crate fails; real crate passes; missing unsafe-ledger row for a hypothetical audited dependency fails (probe with temp registry row/lock edits, restored after);
- VERIFY_SPEC §5.2 updated to describe the implemented checks;
- fast lane green; row-count changes reflected nowhere as hardcoded numbers (none exist).

FUTURE-SELF NOTES
Empty-crate detection is a tripwire, not a proof — the review checklist still owns judgment. Do not let the heuristic grow clever enough to be gamed into a false sense of coverage; keep it visibly dumb and conservative.

title: FG-002: Freeze canonical codec, crypto registry, and typed identities
description:
GOAL
One canonical byte-encoding profile for every immutable FrankenGit body, a versioned domain-separated digest/crypto registry, and typed algorithm-agile identities — without ever rewriting or aliasing native Git OIDs.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Everything downstream — seals, capsules, decisions, RCRs, batches, heads, evidence — derives identity from canonical bytes. If two encoders can produce different bytes for "the same" value, identity splits and the whole authority model (one TxId, one terminal outcome, one head chain) collapses. This is why the plan (§11) demands one deterministic encoding, explicit version/domain/algorithm, canonical ordering, bounded decoding, and golden vectors, and why exactly ONE TxId derivation may exist repo-wide (mechanically enforced by fgit-registry-check). Native Git identity is (GitHashAlgorithm, digest bytes): SHA-1 and SHA-256 are distinct TYPES, never compared by bytes; internal strong digests add evidence but never replace or upgrade Git OIDs (plan §11.2/§11.6).

DESIGN DECISIONS TO MAKE HERE (plan §47 D1)
Compare hand-owned binary framing vs postcard/CBOR-like subsets vs purpose-built codec on: one-byte-string-per-value, bounded decoding, WASM portability, forward compatibility, auditability. Decision lands as an ADR with alternatives and non-claims. No floats, no ambiguous-order maps, no platform-sized integers, no locale, no wall-clock identity inputs.

STRUCTURE
This epic closes when its three subtasks (encoding+goldens; digest/crypto registry; adversarial corpus + independent verifier) are closed and the combined evidence exists.

ACCEPTANCE (epic-level)
- domain/version/length framing and unknown-field rules specified and implemented in fgit-types/fgit-codec;
- unsigned-body vs signature/attestation envelope convention fixed (signatures NEVER inside identity bytes — plan §14.1 precedent);
- SHA-1/SHA-256 Git OIDs remain distinct types from all internal IDs; no API accepts an untyped hash string where two domains are possible;
- golden valid/invalid vectors checked in; independent minimal verifier (separate crate or std-only test binary) validates them;
- algorithm registry supports migration/mixed-version without confusing native Git IDs;
- mutation corpus proves noncanonical encodings never share an identity with canonical ones.

FUTURE-SELF NOTES
This is the deepest possible foundation: get it wrong and every later golden vector churns. Freeze slowly, test violently. The workspace crates here (fgit-types, fgit-codec) are the first engine crates — they must arrive as real vertical slices with tests, not scaffolds (fg001c tripwire will also enforce this).

title: FG-002b: Domain-separated digest/crypto registry and typed OIDs
description:
SCOPE (subtask of fg002-canonical-codec)
The versioned cryptographic registry: algorithm IDs, object-domain separation tags, typed internal ID = (algorithm, domain, codec version, digest bytes); typed native Git OIDs (SHA-1 and SHA-256 as distinct types) kept strictly apart from internal IDs.

WHY THIS SHAPE: domain separation prevents a digest of one object class being replayed as another class (a real cross-protocol attack class); typing prevents the silent SHA-1/SHA-256 byte-aliasing the compatibility matrix explicitly bans. SHA-1 collision defense (plan §11.6): collision-detecting SHA-1 path for Git identity, strong internal payload commitment alongside, fail closed on collision evidence, never invisibly upgrade old signatures.

ACCEPTANCE
- creating an internal ID without a domain tag is unrepresentable in the API;
- cross-domain digest replay produces a typed mismatch in tests;
- Git OID types reject cross-format comparison at compile time; hex parsing requires explicit algorithm context;
- collision-defense hook point exists with a test double (real sha1cd selection is a dependency-registry decision recorded when made);
- registry rows for every algorithm/domain live in code as a closed enum + are exported into the golden corpus so fg002c's independent verifier can check them.

title: FG-002c: Codec mutation/adversarial corpus + independent verifier
description:
SCOPE (subtask of fg002-canonical-codec; test/evidence slice)
An adversarial campaign proving identity cannot be confused: mutation corpus (bit flips, truncations, extensions, reordered fields, duplicated fields, wrong domain tags, wrong versions) over every golden vector, asserting each mutant either decodes to a DIFFERENT identity or refuses — never the same identity; plus an INDEPENDENT minimal verifier (std-only, sharing no code with fgit-codec beyond type definitions) that re-derives digests for all goldens.

WHY INDEPENDENT: a bug shared by encoder and checker is invisible; independence is the point (same doctrine as verifier-independence classes in the agent protocol).

- 100% of goldens verified by the independent verifier;

title: FG-004: AuthorityStore contract, in-memory faultable profile, and history checker
description:
GOAL
The backend-neutral primitive set on which ALL canonical publication rests: strong put-if-absent (seals, immutable bodies), authenticated head read with exact version token, and conditional head replacement (CAS) with monotone generation — specified as a trait (crate fgit-authority), implemented by an in-memory faultable reference backend, and policed by a linearizability history checker.

WHY / BACKGROUND
The entire v3 architecture removed leader/lease/home-cell correctness (NEG-013) and put ALL ordering authority into one conditional primitive. Therefore the primitive's contract must be airtight: ABA protection (a byte-identical restored body must NOT satisfy a CAS expecting the old incarnation — this is exactly the S3 content-derived-ETag hazard, plan §8.5/OSDL), no correctness dependence on listings/notifications/clocks/lease expiry, and read-your-writes for the head key. Backends earn trust ONLY by passing this suite — "S3-compatible" is marketing, not semantics (risk R3).

STRUCTURE: subtasks = (a) trait + contract spec + in-memory faultable impl, (b) linearizability history schema + checker, (c) fault suite.

ACCEPTANCE (epic)
- trait covers put-if-absent, read-with-version-token, conditional-replace-exact-token, monotone generation exposure; explicitly NO list/scan operation in the trait;
- in-memory profile supports scripted fault injection (duplicate responses, lost acks, delayed/stale reads, ambiguous CAS outcomes) for the lab (FG-013 consumes this);
- history checker validates linearizability of recorded histories and rejects seeded violations;
- explicit typed refusal path for backends that cannot prove the contract (used by the future object-store adapter FG-006).

FUTURE-SELF NOTES
Ambiguous CAS response (timeout after send) is NORMAL — the resolution is reread + outcome lookup by TxId, never assume-failed. Encode that in the contract docs and tests now, because every retry bug in the future traces back to this seam.

title: FG-006: Object-store AuthorityStore conformance adapter
description:
GOAL
One provider-neutral adapter exposing the exact AuthorityStore contract over an object-store API (conditional writes / If-Match-class semantics), with the conformance evidence that separates provable backends from marketing.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Hosted/clustered FrankenGit keeps truth in an object store (Cursor-derived insight), but risk R3 is real: nominally S3-compatible backends differ on linearizability, version tokens, gateways, and failover. The adapter must verify version/ETag/conditional semantics EMPIRICALLY per backend and refuse startup on unprovable semantics (fail closed, never degrade silently). ABA: content-derived ETags make byte-identical restores satisfy stale If-Match — so the head body must carry the monotone generation as an independent check, and the adapter must detect and reject token-reuse anomalies.

STRUCTURE: subtasks = (a) adapter over a minimal owned HTTP/signing surface (Asupersync-based, no cloud SDK — DEP-010), (b) Jepsen-style fault campaign using the FG-004b checker.

ACCEPTANCE (epic)
- capability receipt records exact API/region/configuration probed;
- concurrent histories over injected faults pass the linearizability checker for a claimed-conformant backend profile;
- unsupported semantics -> typed startup refusal;
- no bucket listing participates in truth or recovery;
- adapter dependency surface is registry-approved (no SDK, no Tokio-transitive).

FUTURE-SELF NOTES

title: FG-007: Transaction seal, stable TxId, and terminal outcome lookup
description:
GOAL
Implement the sole normative transaction identity (the single TxId derivation defined once in docs/NORMATIVE_PROTOCOL_CONTRACTS.md — the checker enforces its uniqueness repo-wide), the permanent semantic request seal, and terminal-outcome lookup that survives crashes and accelerator loss.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Retry ambiguity is the root pathology of distributed mutation. The seal converts "a network attempt" into "a logical mutation with one stable identity": put-if-absent on canonicalized semantic bytes; byte-identical body -> idempotent retry continuing the same transaction; different body under the same idempotency key -> typed IdempotencyKeyReuse rejection. Crucially (v3 audit fix): admission capability, policy epoch, and first-seen time are SEPARATE admission receipts over the seal ID, NOT seal-body fields — otherwise a legitimate retry could never regenerate identical bytes. There is NO canonical Cancelled terminal: client cancellation/disconnect never proves non-commit; the client queries the outcome index by TxId.

STRUCTURE: subtasks = (a) implementation, (b) race/crash campaign.

ACCEPTANCE (epic)
- same principal/repository/idempotency-key/body -> one TxId across retries; different body -> typed conflict;
- pre-seal rejection distinguished from post-seal canonical refusal (only the latter enters DecisionSequence);
- outcome lookup works after crash and accelerator loss by replaying the decision stream (accelerators are rebuildable, never authoritative — plan §15.8);
- concurrent commit/refusal races publish at most one terminal decision (property inherited from FG-003, proven here against real storage).

title: FG-008: Intent evaluation and net-effect normal form
description:
GOAL
The intent -> effect -> net-effect pipeline (FrankenGraphDB-inherited): ordered statements of typed intents evaluated with read-your-own-writes against one pinned basis, folded into target-disjoint canonical effects, with every source intent mapped to a surviving effect or an explicit no-op/error/abort.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Clients — human or agent — must not be able to lie (even accidentally) about cascades, prior values, deletion sets, or ordering. title: FG-010: Checkpoint, capsule, backup, and restore body formats
description:

Publication: stage -> verify -> satisfy placement obligations -> hash body -> sign -> conditionally publish pointer for that exact head -> only then retention-review superseded material. description:
GOAL

title: FG-012: Obligation-typed canonical and external effects
description:
GOAL
Every effect that acquires responsibility — object staging, head publication, outbox delivery, package/release upload, secret leases, workspace outputs, repair writes, agent effects — becomes a typed obligation with the normative lifecycle: Reserved to Committed to Acknowledged, or Reserved to Aborted. Fire-and-forget is not a state.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Cancellation correctness is impossible when effects are untracked: a dropped future holding a half-sent webhook or an un-reaped runner is silent corruption of the outside world. The CALM/obligation doctrine (docs/CALM_AND_OBLIGATIONS.md) makes ownership structural: must_use obligations, region close requiring settle-or-explicit-transfer, and — for externally observed effects — a distinct Acknowledged stage: commit makes the effect canonically owned; acknowledgement separately records that the recipient observed it; post-commit retry is idempotent; region close either records acknowledgement or leaves an explicit unacknowledged-effect record, never silence. The CALM registry (registries/calm_operations.tsv, 7-class closed vocabulary) determines WHERE coordination is required; obligations determine WHO owns unfinished work.

STRUCTURE: subtasks = (a) obligation core + concrete obligation types, (b) quiescence oracle + lab evidence.

ACCEPTANCE (epic)
- core obligation types from CALM section 7 exist with the trait shape from CALM section 6 (Obligation::commit yields CommittedObligation; abort; Acknowledge trait for the ack stage): ObjectAdmissionPermit, PreparedTxnSlot, HeadCasAttempt, OutboxEffectPermit, SecretLease, WorkspaceLease, RunnerSlot, RetentionPin, RepairPermit, ContextBudgetPermit, BillingReservation;
- every reserved effect reaches committed/aborted/terminally-quarantined before region close; dropping without transfer/commit/abort is a lab correctness failure and a typed production containment event;
- external APIs with weak idempotency get an explicit reconciliation state machine;
- obligation ledger replayable and linked to TxId/IntentRun;
- CALM registry class consulted for coordination decisions (a monotone op never takes the head CAS path; a head_cas_required op cannot bypass it — both directions fixture-tested, proving registry rows are load-bearing).

title: FG-017: Deterministic pack planning and writing
description:
GOAL
Generate compatible packs from canonical objects without upstream Git: reachability closure, deterministic object ordering, delta candidate selection with a named tie-break policy, and receipted planning.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Serving clone/fetch requires producing packs every Git client accepts. Determinism is the differentiator: a deterministic baseline profile (same inputs, same bytes) makes caching/sharing/compaction trustworthy (plan section 17.5, compute-once-share-by-profile) and keeps evidence replayable; any future non-deterministic optimization profile must be EXPLICIT, never the silent default. Cancellation must never leave a partial pack anywhere a consumer could mistake for complete.

STRUCTURE: subtasks = (a) planner/writer implementation, (b) validation + benchmark evidence.

ACCEPTANCE (epic)
- planning receipts capture closure inputs, ordering policy, delta candidates/tie-breaks, bitmap/commit-graph inputs;
- output validates through the independent fg016 reader AND pinned Git clients;

title: FG-029: Canonical forge events and atomic pull-request merge
description:

title: FG-037: Verified-read inclusion proofs (trustless serving)

title: FG-043: Policy snapshots, policy language, protected refs, and break glass
description:
GOAL
The deterministic authorization/policy engine (plan section 32): compiled content-addressed PolicySnapshots, a declarative bounded policy language, the full protected-ref rule vocabulary, break-glass overrides, and simulation/shadow/warn/enforce rollout modes.

WHY / BACKGROUND
Canonical policy evaluation is deterministic over one named input root (plan 15.9): no wall clock, no unversioned external services, no model output during publication — external checks enter as signed typed evidence receipts with explicit acceptance/expiry rules. Break glass (32.5): named reason, stronger auth, threshold approval, narrow scope, immutable audit, notification, post-review, displaced-state retention — and it can never disable evidence of its own use.

title: FG-046: Webhook delivery product over the transactional outbox
description:
GOAL
Webhook delivery as a product (plan 31.5, v1 scope item 9): canonical delivery intents from the outbox, signed payloads, stable idempotency/delivery IDs, bounded retry schedules, replay, dead-letter inspection, secret rotation, and tenant egress policy.

WHY / BACKGROUND

title: FG-059: Repository incarnations, rename/delete lifecycle, and migration protocol
description:
GOAL
The identity lifecycle machinery of plan 11.1 and 37.5: typed repository incarnations (delete/recreate under the same owner/name creates a NEW incarnation; nothing stale can revive the prior one), rename/transfer flows, logical-vs-physical deletion states surfaced to users (19.4), and backend/namespace migration as a capsule/authority protocol — never "move the home cell".

WHY / BACKGROUND
Incarnation confusion is a real attack/bug class: stale tokens, caches, federation events, webhooks, or object-location records pointing at a deleted-then-recreated name must NOT act on the new repository. Every canonical record already binds the incarnation ID (fg002 schemas); this bead builds the lifecycle: creation mints an incarnation, deletion tombstones it through retention/grace machinery (fg033), recreation mints a fresh one, and all resolution paths (API, transports, webhooks, caches) check incarnation match. Migration (37.5): repository moves between backends/deployments via export-capsule + restore + conditional routing publication — the routing flip is itself a coordinated decision with anti-rollback, and the source enters a typed read-only-then-tombstone sequence.

ACCEPTANCE
- stale-reference corpus: pre-deletion tokens/webhooks/caches against a recreated name all refuse typed (incarnation mismatch);
- rename keeps incarnation (aliases recorded); transfer across owners keeps incarnation with an audit event;
- migration drill: export, restore to a second deployment, routing flip, source freeze — client-observable cutover is atomic (old name serves until flip, then redirects/refuses per policy);
- deletion states surfaced distinctly (hidden / tombstoned-in-grace / authorized / deleted-hot / expired-everywhere / crypto-erased).

TEST PLAN: lifecycle unit tests; e2e scripts/e2e/incarnation_migration.sh (delete/recreate probes + full migration drill) registered in run_all.sh.

title: FG-065: Hosted multi-tenant operations — evacuation, capacity, incident modes
description:

A toolchain advancement is a MATERIAL change (AGENTS.md 3.4): the pinned nightly is refreshed frequently but only by an explicit commit whose evidence pack proves behavior and performance did not regress. fg061's D15 ADR records the CADENCE POLICY; this bead builds the LANE that executes it — distinct from the checker (fg001x, which validates the pin is dated) and release (fg035). - a seeded regression (e.g. a new clippy denial or a perf threshold breach) refuses the bump with typed evidence;

title: FG-072: Verifier-independence classification and enforcement
description:
GOAL
The typed verifier-independence machinery AGENT_PROTOCOL.md:94-104 defines: classify producer/verifier pairs across seven independence dimensions, evaluate per-risk-class policy on which dimensions MUST differ, refuse with IndependentVerificationRequired when they do not, and detect collusion/shared-hidden-state.

WHY / BACKGROUND
"Independence is a typed evidence class, not self-declaration" (:94). Dimensions: mutable workspace; credentials and effect authority; model/harness implementation; supplied context and hidden state; oracle/toolchain; operator/organization; human oversight. Policy states which must differ per risk class. fg030b builds the Evidence-Carrying Change with an independence CLASSIFIER, but this bead is the ENFORCEMENT ENGINE and its adversarial corpus: "producer and verifier may collude or share hidden state" (:41) is a named threat, and conformance item 8 (:681) is "producer/verifier trust-domain classification tests". A verifier sharing the producer's workspace or credentials is automatically non-independent; the risk-class policy decides whether that is fatal. This is the machinery that makes agent-generated evidence trustworthy instead of self-attested.

DELIVERABLES: the seven-dimension independence type; per-risk-class required-difference policy (integrates with fg043); the evaluator producing an independence verdict with the differing/shared dimensions named; collusion detection (shared workspace/credential/hidden-state fingerprints); the refusal path.

description:

title: FG-086: External head-continuity witness profile
description:
GOAL
The optional external anti-rollback defense OBJECT_STORE_DECISION_LOG.md section 15 (line 434) offers: independent continuity witnesses that pin recent head IDs for high-value repositories, defending against a storage backend that serves an old-but-valid head.

WHY / BACKGROUND
This is a "may" in the doc (high-value repositories only), which is why it is P3 — but it is a real, tracked defense that would otherwise be lost. fg009b campaigns anti-rollback INTERNALLY (the recovery logic refuses ambiguous newest state); but if the authority backend itself is compromised or buggy and serves a stale-but-authenticated head, internal logic alone cannot detect it — an INDEPENDENT witness that has seen head N refuses to accept a subsequent read claiming head N-k. This complements fg037 (verified reads let CLIENTS check answers against a head) by letting the SYSTEM check the head itself against an external attestation. Depends on fg009 (head chain) and relates to fg036 (distributed) where multiple cells can cross-witness.

DELIVERABLES: a continuity-witness record (repository, highest-seen head id + generation + timestamp-as-data, witness identity/signature); a witness-check hook in authority reads for high-value repositories; the refusal path when a read regresses below a witnessed generation; multi-witness quorum option (cells cross-witnessing in fg036 deployments).

ACCEPTANCE
- a stale-head read below a witnessed generation is refused with typed rollback evidence;
- witnesses are advisory-to-availability but authoritative-to-safety (a missing witness degrades availability per policy, never accepts a rollback);
- multi-witness quorum drill in a multi-cell deployment;
- opt-in per repository (high-value only) with clear cost documentation.

- Asupersync is the sole async runtime (no Tokio/async-std/smol). Long-lived work owns children via regions; cancellation is request -> drain -> finalize; effects use typed obligations (Reserved -> Committed -> Acknowledged, or Reserved -> Aborted).
- Closed dependency universe: every crate (incl. transitive, enforced via Cargo.lock scan) must match an active allow row in registries/dependency_policy.tsv. No build scripts/proc macros without a constitutional exception. No network during builds.
- Final-abstraction slices only: no empty crates, no HashMap-pretending-to-be-storage, no fixture-only parser wired as production API. A subset is fine when its unsupported surface is a typed refusal.
- Claim lattice (invariant > proof > bounded model > statistical > SLO > benchmark): never describe this work as stronger than its evidence. Record disproven hypotheses in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md + registries/negative_evidence.tsv.
- Run ./scripts/verify.sh fast before and after; stage only intended files; keep generated artifacts out of source.
